headline: National MUSEUMS 🏛️ STAY FREE 💸 for ALL 🌍 Visitors FOREVER 🕰️
text:
National MUSEUMS 🏛️ are gonna STAY 🛡️ free 🎟️ for EVERYONE 👥 after the government 🏛️ decided against CHARGING 💰 overseas tourists 🧳 to BOOST 📈 those finances 💵!! It follows MONTHS 🗓️ of heated talks 🗣️ between ministers 👔 museums 🏛️ the tourism 🧳 sector and local leaders 👑 to see if making foreigners pay 💸 could help with funding pressures 🥴 but nah they ultimately said it would DETER 🚫 domestic visitors 🏠 and the benefits wouldn't hit every institution the SAME ⚖️ so they're keeping that UNIVERSAL FREE 🎟️ admission policy locked in since 2001 📅!!

In MARCH 🌼 the government said they'd explore CHARGING 💰 international visitors 🧳 to tackle those funding squeezes 💸 but the DEPARTMENT 📋 for Digital Culture Media and Sport has now confirmed this could SCARE OFF 😱 homegrown crowds and any cash gains wouldn't spread equally across the SECTOR 🏛️!! The UK's 15 NATIONAL MUSEUMS 🏛️ including 12 in LONDON 🏙️ have been FREE 🎟️ for all since 2001 and a review by former Labour minister Baroness Margaret Hodge suggested charging tourists would align the UK with places like New Zealand 🇳🇿 and Singapore 🇸🇬 but on TUESDAY 📅 DCMS shut it down HARD 🛑 and confirmed free admission remains for EVERYONE 👥!!

The government SPOKESPERSON 🗣️ dropped the official word saying charging overseas visitors could DETER 🚫 domestic ones and impacts wouldn't be felt equally so they will NOT introduce charges for overseas visitors period!! Culture secretary LISA NANDY 👩‍💼 said our museums are the places that LIGHT UP 💡 the world and that's why they must be FREE 🎟️ forever for everyone to access no ifs ands or BUTS 🛡️!! The DCMS pointed out these national museums pump more than one BILLION POUNDS 💷 into the economy every year and pull in global crowds 🌍 with the Natural History Museum 🦕 hitting 7.1 million visitors and the British Museum 🏛️ at 6.4 million in 2025 alone!!

Natural History Museum director Dr Doug Gurr admitted his spot would've BENEFITED 💰 from charging but the whole sector would've LOST OUT 📉 overall and stressed that free museums aren't a cost to the economy they're actually a KEY REASON 🗝️ the economy benefits from tourism in the first place so they're delighted to remain FREE 🎟️ but still made the case for reinvesting some tourism revenues back into the institutions that help ATTRACT them 🧲!! Nicholas Cullinan director of the British Museum reminded everyone that when it was founded in 1753 as the world's first public national museum it was meant to be free for ALL PERSONS 👥 so they're delighted by the government's announcement that free entry for all will be maintained allowing everyone to enjoy these great museums as one of the things this country does so BRILLIANTLY ⭐!!

The government also highlighted 760 million pounds in funding for museums through its 1.5 billion Arts Everywhere Fund plus 600 million in infrastructure cash for national museums and the 13.6 million museum transformation programme to help organizations move toward more sustainable business models while they work with the Arts Council on a long-term strategic plan with more details coming soon!! Overall the decision keeps those Egyptian sculptures 🗿 and everything else at the British Museum accessible without any tourist TAX 💸 so the whole scene stays open and welcoming like it has been for DECADES 🕰️!!
